Gaining Mutations

Gaining more Corruption points than the sum of your Willpower Bonus and Toughness Bonus forces you to pass a Challenging (+0) Endurance Test or gain a mutation. If you fail the Test, consult the table below to see if the nature of your corruption is mental or physical.

If you gain the physical corruption you reduce your Corruption points equal to your Toughness Bonus. For mental corruption you reduce them equal to your Willpower Bonus.

Physical Corruption

Physical corruption manifests as alterations of the flesh of the unfortunate, or blessed depending on your perspective, and they range from relatively superficial changes to deeply unnatural transformations.

Mental Corruption

Mental corruption twists the mind, introducing strange new thoughts and desires. It may start as curious but relatively harmless ideas and behaviours. Over time however, as corruption accumulates, the curious gives way to the weird and the heinous as the pain and confusion gives way to strange new ways of thinking and powerful abilities. While mental corruption may initially be easier to conceal than physical, the deteriorating level of self-control and the blooming dark cravings, challenges the ability of the afflicted to conform with social convention - risking the attention from the witch hunters.

Corruption vs Mental Illness

Portraying mental illness in role-playing games can be sensitive and difficult. This supplement has no ambition of representing real-life mental illness in a realistic way. The intention is to capture a core theme of the WFRP setting - facing Lovecraftian horrors and the inevitable terror of having your own mind betray you as a result of the corrupting influence of those horrors. Corruption is an external force twisting the body, mind and soul - and the symptoms that arise from that.

Contemporary terminology (like schizoid, phobia or psychosis) has been avoided as much as possible when describing these mental symptoms, and they are cinematic simplifications meant to fit a world beset by daemons and undead.

It’s recommended that the GM discuss mental corruption in a session zero so that the group can voice any concerns and together decide how you portray it.

Mutation Severity

Once it’s established the nature of your corruption, consult the table below to determine the severity of your mutation. Add +10 on the roll for every mutation your Character already has up to your 4th mutation (making it a maximum of +40). Lastly, roll on the respective mutation table in the next chapter - A Catalogue of Change - to see which specific mutation you will develop.

Mutation Severity Table

1d100

Severity

1-60

Trivial Mutation

61-100

Minor Mutation

101-130

Major Mutation

131+

Chosen of Chaos

You may spend a Resilience point to avoid developing a mutation. If you do so, you still reduce your Corruption points as described above. You may roll first to see which mutation you would gain before spending your Resilience point.

Trivial Mutations

While trivial mutations can be horrific changes for the individual they are alterations that often, with some discretion, are possible to hide. Most people with Trivial Mutations are able to keep on living in society.

Minor Mutations

Minor mutations are more transformative and as such harder to conceal, but also tend to provide more modifiers and abilities. Minor mutations will be recognized on sight, either as the blasphemous corruption of Chaos they are (physical mutations) or as madness (mental mutations).

Major Mutations

Major mutations are typically very transformative and much harder to conceal, but may also offer powerful modifiers and abilities. On exposure these mutations are immediately recognizable as the corruption of Chaos.

Chosen of Chaos

If you roll the Chosen of Chaos result you have become blessed by one of The Chaos Gods.

While this is great news if you’re a Slave to Darkness it most likely means that this is a good time to create a new Character… unless your GM is running a campaign where he’s fine with you championing the Ruinous Powers from the edge of society.

If the latter is the case, consider picking up the Tome of Corruption for 2e and the homebrew  Warriors of Chaos supplement. In the appendix of this supplement you’ll find mutation tables for the respective chaos patron that can be used instead of those mentioned in the Tome of Corruption.

Manifestation

While some mutations can erupt suddenly from the body or mind as full blown mutations, it’s more common that they develop over time.  The itching growth on the stomach that one day opens up as a glaring eye, or the building desire to taste rotten flesh that eventually climaxes in a dark and shameful feast. If the Players want there are ample opportunities to make the dissolution of body and mind part of the story and not just about modifiers and abilities.

Mutation Levels

Gaining the same mutation more than once will add the same modifiers again unless stated otherwise in the description of the mutation.

Talents that you gain through mutations gain another level and the Difficulty of any Tests is increased (for resisting negative mutation effects) or decreased (for activating abilities) by one degree. For example, if a Mutation provides a +10 Toughness Bonus, the same modifiers would apply again when rolling the same result again on the table. The GM determines how that manifests in the actual Mutation.

Negative Modifiers

Several mutations provide negative modifiers for Characteristics. You can never decrease lower than 0. Ignore further negative modifiers for that attribute.

Corruption Limits

If you gain more physical mutations than your Toughness Bonus or more mental mutations than your Willpower Bonus, the corruption has ravaged your mortal shell beyond its limits and you become a mindless Chaos Spawn.

Chaos Spawn

As Chaos Spawns are mindless beasts it’s time to roll a new Character and hope you never meet whatever became of the old one… The Chaos Spawn are described in more detail in the Tome of Corruption.

Reactions to Mutations

Tolerable

Some of mutations, like Hairless, Hunchback, Morbidity and Hateful Impulses, are a bit odd but don't stand out enough to brand you a mutant. People might react with suspicion or disgust, but not with alarm. These mutations are labelled Tolerable and generally provide a negative Fellowship modifier, but do not cause @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.Item.Q2MCUrG2HppMcvN0]{Animosity} or @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.Item.Ib2YQYChktDFN93y]{Fear}.

Keep in mind that The Old World is a setting that, while having deep distrust for the abnormal and corrupt, is riddled with people who display odd appearances and behaviours. In a world where healthcare is very limited the effects of disease, hard physical labour, terrifying dangers and violence provide plenty of disfigured and traumatised people to blend in among.

Trivial

If ordinary folks are exposed to trivial mutations they gain @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.Item.klCJX0mNpXYH5AIx]{Prejudice (Mutants)} at an Average (+20) Difficulty unless stated otherwise in the description of the mutation. Mental mutations may cause @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.Item.klCJX0mNpXYH5AIx]{Prejudice (Mad Men)} at The GM’s discretion. Make the Difficulty one step worse per non-tolerable mutation being exposed.

Minor

Ordinary people that are being exposed to minor mutations gain @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.Item.Q2MCUrG2HppMcvN0]{Animosity (Mutants)} at an Average (+20) Difficulty unless stated otherwise in the description of the mutation.

Make the Difficulty one step worse per non-tolerable mutation being exposed.

Minor mental mutations are typically only noticed when you lose self control and start behaving well beyond the social norm, like with Bizarre Denial, Unending Malice or Touched. Depending on the situation some people may call it corruption whereas others call it madness. If the latter is the case they gain @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.Item.klCJX0mNpXYH5AIx]{Prejudice (Mad Men)} instead of @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.Item.Q2MCUrG2HppMcvN0]{Animosity (Mutants)}.

Major

When ordinary people are exposed to major mutations they are subject to @Fear[1] unless stated otherwise in the description of the mutation. Some major mental mutations only cause fear when others can perceive them. If a mutation causes Fear of a higher level, or Terror, then that takes precedence. The effects do not stack.

Concealment

The first impulse of any civilised individual gaining a mutation is likely to hide it from view, lest the witch hunters eradicate you. Luckily people tend to clothe most of their bodies in everyday situations as modesty and chastity are valued traits in The Old World.

Trivial physical mutations are generally Easy (+40) to conceal, like an Additional Appendage, Beastial Feature or Extra Joints.

Minor physical mutations can often be concealed, although typically at Challenging (+0) Difficulty.

Major physical mutations tend to be Very Hard (-30) or impossible to conceal, like Additional Extremities, or Burning Body.

Self-Control

Mental corruptions that cause behavioural changes (like Urgent Profanity) or negative effects (like Pyrokinesis) can be suppressed for a scene (see Social Interaction) with a successful Challenging (+0) Cool Test to avoid drawing unwanted attention - unless stated otherwise in the description of the mutation. You cannot suppress effects that affect your Characteristics or modify Tests or provide Creature Traits (like Aethyric Leak, Hubris and Hungering Maw).

The Difficulty is Average (+20) for Trivial mutations, Challenging (+0) for Minor and Difficult (-10) for Major.  The Difficulty is increased by one step per level you have in the mutation. If you fail the roll you may choose to spend Resolve to suppress the mutation anyway.

Player Agency

Mental corruption can be tricky to implement in the game as it impacts a core tenet of what makes role-playing games fun - player agency. It’s recommended that, while the GM presents the challenge, it’s the Players who own how their Character acts. For example, if a Player fails a Cool Test for controlling their Bizarre Denial or Dark Appetite , it’s up to them to describe how their Player acts out their corruption - not the GM. Also, don’t have the Players make Tests for self-control all the time, that’s just tedious. Choose situations when it really matters - make it count - and where a failure can spawn intriguing circumstances!

While there is no unified, scientific method of dealing with mutation in the Old World, there are those willing to offer treatment. Treatments are often expensive as the clients tend to be desperate and need both discretion and cutting edge remedies.

Surgery

It is possible to find discreet physicians who out of compassion, greed or curiosity treat physical mutations. Among the upper echelons of society, where people have both status and gold, it’s not unknown to go on a prolonged retreat in some remote area and come back with renewed vigour and confidence, much like the family of a young noblewoman might do if she were to become pregnant before she’s been married away.

The GM will decide the Difficulty of the surgery. Cutting of a stray finger is probably Very Easy (+60) whereas removing a vestigial twin is Very Hard (-30), and a glowing heart or blob-form impossible. Consult the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.Item.NP4EHyyh1yOLbsPU]{Surgery} Talent regarding the procedure and the table below to determine the result. In some cases, a body part might need to be @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.journals.JournalEntry.NS3YGlJQxwTggjRX.JournalEntryPage.WCivInLZrqEtZzF4#amputated-parts]{amputated}. At The GM’s discretion the mutation may eventually grow back even if the surgery was successful.

Surgery Table

SL

Result

-6

We’ve got a bleeder! The patient dies on the operating table.

-4 to -5

Crippling failure. The mutation remains and your Strength, Toughness, and Agility are reduced by -1d10 each.

-2 to -3

Painful failure. The mutation remains and your Toughness is reduced by -1d10.

-1 to -0

Failure. The mutation remains, but you don’t suffer any additional trauma.

0 to +1

Partial success. Some part of your mutation was removed. The GM decides what that means in practice.

+2 to +3

Solid success! The mutation is removed!

+4 to +5

Impressive success! The mutation is removed and you don’t get a @Condition[Bleeding] Condition or an Infection.

+6

A surgical triumph! The goal is achieved with no complications, you don’t get a @Condition[Bleeding] Condition or an Infection. Your recovery time is halved.

Asylum & Hospice

Many of the trivial and minor mental mutations can be mistaken for ordinary mental trauma and madness - something which some open minded institutions offer treatment for. For the wealthy who have the means to pay for admission to an asylum, it’s not uncommon to have a relative admitted to calm their nerves.  The asylums are often found in the cities.

The Healing Order of the Sisters of Shallya provides hospices, hospital-monasteries, throughout the Empire to help the poor and sick. These often lie somewhat secluded, away from the bustling cities.

Admitted Character’s may undertake a Regimen Endeavour in an attempt to fortify themselves against their mental corruption, or maybe even cure it. If you pass a Very Hard (-30) Cool Test the level of mental corruption is reduced by 1. You need +6 SL to completely remove a mental corruption however (go from 1 to 0 levels). At The GM’s discretion the mutation may eventually return even if the Regimen was successful.

Drugs

Apothecaries and herbalists are happy to sell remedies. The GM decides which drugs are effective for which type of mental mutation - perhaps Nightshade will help against Chaotic Nightmares for instance. If you want a more generic solution you can buy a week's worth of curatives for 2 GC that will reduce the Difficulty of any self-control Test by one level.

Indulgence

While it certainly won’t lead to a cure, indulging your trivial or minor mental mutation can help alleviate some of its everyday pressure. The GM determines what you need at hand, and if you have to spend some coin in order to indulge your mutation.

For example: Someone with a Dark Appetite may lock themselves in and feast, whereas someone with a Fixation could haunt the local library.

If you undertake an Indulgence Endeavour and pass a Challenging (+0) Cool Test you may reduce the difficulty by one level for the coming SL days when you need to do a self-control Test for that particular corruption. Critical failure on the Cool Test causes you some sort of problem of The GM’s choosing as you stare too deep into the abyss; like forgetting about other Endeavours or offending someone
